catalog_entry.label: MLB Draft pick position markets
catalog_entry.target: Whether a named prospect is selected at an exact overall pick or within the top N picks of the MLB Draft.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The MLB Draft is a sequential without-replacement selection. The order of clubs at slots 1-10 is fixed by the lottery (picks 1-6), reverse prior-season record, luxury-tax pick moves and inserted compensation picks, and first-round picks cannot be traded. Each club then takes the highest player on its own board after adjusting for its bonus pool strategy, its front-office tendency and each prospect's medicals and signability; many top picks are pre-agreed below slot. A prospect's slot is therefore the outcome of consensus talent rank, club-specific deviation and the cascade of choices ahead of him.

inputs.why: Club identity at each overall slot conditions every exact-slot probability.
Lottery draws set picks 1-6 before the order is known; needed for markets priced before the lottery.
Mean and spread of public board ranks locate the prospect's likely selection window.
Final mocks and pre-draft bonus agreement reports link the prospect to a club and slot.
Weights each insider's club-player link by that source's historical accuracy.
Shows which kinds of clubs value the prospect above or below consensus.
Medical flags and bonus demands drive draft-day slides below talent rank.
Club-specific preference decides whether the club at a slot takes the consensus player.
Pool budget and underslot incentives explain picks that depart from talent order.
Structural requirement, not an information source: the without-replacement engine that keeps exact-slot and top-10 probabilities consistent across prospects.
Clubs far over the top tax threshold have their first pick moved back ten slots.
A lockout after the CBA expiry could postpone or reshape the next draft.
Defines exact-slot versus top-N construction and which draft year counts.

interactions.hypothesis: A prospect's exact-slot chance depends on whether the club at that slot historically prefers his profile, so the same board rank gives different slot odds under different orders.
Insider links carry most information when boards disagree; when boards agree tightly, reports add little beyond the consensus rank.
Clubs pursuing underslot deals favour low-leverage college seniors, so high-demand prep players slide further at slots held by pool-constrained clubs.
A medical or bonus-demand flag moves a top-three prospect little but pushes a prospect ranked 6-12 out of the top 10, so the slide depends on consensus rank.

contract.settlement_definition: KXMLBDRAFTPICK settles YES only if the named prospect is selected at the stated overall slot (sample: 5th overall) in the stated draft year; KXMLBDRAFTTOP settles YES if he is selected at any slot within the top N (sample: top 10) of that draft. Selection, not signing, is what the text names, so an unsigned pick still appears to count. The text names no source of truth, does not say whether inserted compensation picks are numbered as overall picks, and says nothing about a postponed or cancelled draft.

rules_evidence.quote: If Zion Rose is selected as the 5th overall pick in the 2026 Pro Baseball Draft, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-slot construction on the overall pick number, tied to one draft year; selection event, not signing.

rules_evidence.quote: If Zion Rose is drafted top 10 in the 2026 Pro Baseball Draft
rules_evidence.establishes: Cumulative construction over picks up to 10; 'top 10' appears to include the 10th pick but inclusivity is not spelled out.

variants_and_edge_cases: Exact-slot (KXMLBDRAFTPICK) versus cumulative top-N (KXMLBDRAFTTOP): for one prospect the exact-slot probabilities over 1..10 must sum to the top-10 probability.

Inserted round-1 compensation picks for prior-year unsigned first-rounders can change which club holds a given overall number; Prospect Promotion Incentive picks are understood to be placed after round 1 and so not to renumber slots 1-10 (CBA text unverified); whether Kalshi counts inserted picks as overall picks is unstated.
A prospect who is drafted but does not sign appears to satisfy 'selected'/'drafted'; signing is not mentioned.
No clause covers a postponed, shortened or cancelled draft (as in 2020) or a prospect withdrawing or being ruled ineligible before the draft.
rules_secondary is empty for both sampled markets, so no resolution source is named.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules text; presumably the official MLB draft results (MLB.com draft tracker / MLB Stats API draft endpoint).

mechanism.summary: Where a prospect is drafted is decided by a sequence of club choices, not by one event. First the slot-to-club map is fixed: a lottery among non-playoff clubs sets picks 1-6, the rest of the non-playoff clubs follow in reverse record, luxury-tax penalties move some clubs back, compensation picks are inserted, and first-round picks cannot be traded, so the map is known before the draft. Each club then values prospects from its own board, built from tools, performance and tracking data, and adjusts for medicals, bonus demands and its bonus-pool plan; many top picks are agreed below slot in advance and leaked by insiders. The named player's slot is where the first club that most prefers him among those still available chooses him. Exact-slot contracts are sharp point masses within this cascade; top-10 contracts are the cumulative sum.

stages.name: Slot-to-club map
stages.description: The lottery draws picks 1-6 among the 18 non-playoff clubs with odds weighted toward the worst records and eligibility restrictions on repeat winners; remaining non-playoff clubs fill the following slots in reverse record; a club $40M or more over the base luxury-tax threshold has its highest pick moved back ten slots; prior-year failed-to-sign compensation picks are inserted. No first-round trades are allowed, so after the order is published this stage is deterministic.
stages.distribution: Discrete lottery permutation before the draw (multinomial over six slots), degenerate after the official order is published.

stages.name: Prospect valuation and consensus
stages.description: Clubs and public evaluators rank the class from tool grades, opponent-adjusted college or showcase performance, tracked exit velocity, swing decisions or pitch quality, and age relative to class. Public boards are correlated with club boards; the mean rank sets the centre of the selection window and cross-board disagreement sets its width. Rankings move with spring performance, injuries and showcase results, so the board vintage matters.
stages.distribution: Rank variable with heteroscedastic spread: tight for the top two or three prospects, widening sharply beyond about the fifth.

stages.name: Club-specific deviation: tendency, pool and signability
stages.description: Each club deviates from consensus according to its front-office preferences (college bats, prep arms), its bonus-pool plan (underslot at the top to fund later overslot picks), and each prospect's medical flags and bonus demand backed by college commitment. These deviations are persistent within a scouting-director regime and are the main reason exact slots differ from board order.
stages.distribution: Club-level random effects plus a left-skewed slide tail for flagged or high-demand players; occasional large reaches by underslot clubs.

stages.name: Pre-draft agreements and insider information
stages.description: In the final days clubs narrow to a few players and often agree bonuses with advisors before the pick; national writers publish final mocks and club-player links. These reports are the most informative signal for exact slots near the top, but writers differ in accuracy and late changes happen on draft night, so each link must be timestamped and weighted by source track record.
stages.distribution: Information arrives in jumps; slot probabilities concentrate quickly in the final 24-48 hours, with residual surprise from draft-night changes.

stages.name: Sequential selection cascade and settlement
stages.description: Picks are made in order without replacement: the named player is taken at slot k only if no earlier club took him and the club at k prefers him to everyone remaining. Upsets ahead shift him down; reaches ahead shift him up. The exact-slot contract settles on a single overall number and the top-10 contract on the cumulative event; the draft itself could be disrupted by a labour stoppage only for 2027-draft series (CBA expires 1 December 2026).
stages.distribution: Joint without-replacement distribution over prospects and slots; exact slot is a sharp, multi-modal point mass; cumulative top-N is monotone in N.

talent_strength.note: Talent is the prospect's projected value as judged by boards and his performance profile.

opponent_matchup.note: No contest takes place: the draft is a selection among clubs, and competition between clubs for a player is handled by the sequential selection model, not an opponent matchup.

role_personnel.note: Which club sits at each slot and the prospect's position and class profile.

availability_news.note: Medical reports, bonus demands and insider club links with source weighting.

coaching_scheme.note: Front-office and scouting-director drafting philosophy plays the role of scheme.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel do not affect club selections on draft night; park and conference context of prospect stats is adjusted inside the performance profile.

game_context_script.note: The in-draft state (who has been taken before each slot) is the analogue of game script and drives cascades. Structural requirement (derived model), not an information source; the only live in-draft state is the list of picks already made.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities: each slot is one selection, and the number of picks before the threshold is fixed by the contract (5th, top 10).

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity success rate exists; the outcome is an ordinal selection, not a conversion of attempts, so efficiency has no meaning here.

distribution_variance.note: Joint without-replacement slot distribution with cascade dependence. Structural requirement (derived model), not an information source; the only live in-draft state is the list of picks already made.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Pool incentives for underslot picks and labour calendar risk to the draft.

officiating_rules.note: Lottery, order, tax-penalty and compensation-pick rules.

settlement_contract.note: Exact overall slot versus top-N cumulative wording; source and compensation-pick numbering unresolved.

mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.label: Final first-round draft order: which club holds each overall slot 1-10 after lottery, reverse-record fill, CBT pick moves and inserted compensation picks
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.mechanism: An exact-slot contract is a statement about the club holding that slot, so the slot-to-club map must be resolved before any prospect preference applies.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.rationale: The lottery fixes picks 1-6 only; slots 7-18 follow reverse record among non-playoff clubs that missed the lottery, a club far over the top luxury-tax threshold has its first pick moved back ten places (outside the top six), and a prior-year unsigned first-rounder yields an inserted compensation pick one slot later, which renumbers every later pick. First-round picks cannot be traded in MLB, so unlike other leagues the map is fixed once these rules run.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.measurement: Procedure for the draft year: (1) assign picks 1-6 by the published lottery odds for non-playoff clubs; before the lottery output P(club holds slot k) from 10,000 simulations; (2) apply the CBA's lottery-restriction placement for ineligible clubs (verify numeric rule against the CBA text); (3) fill remaining slots by reverse prior-season winning percentage among non-playoff clubs with the official tiebreak; (4) move the highest pick of clubs over the CBT draft-penalty tier back ten places unless it is a top-6 pick (verify tier against the CBA); (5) insert compensation picks for unsigned previous-year first-rounders at original slot + 1 and renumber. Output club_id per overall slot with the official order release timestamp. Every item marked verify must be checked against CBA text before use.
mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment.why: Slot 5 YES requires the specific club at slot 5 to choose the named player, so the club identity at each slot is the first conditioning variable.

mlb.prospect_consensus_board.label: Consensus pre-draft prospect ranking: mean and dispersion of the named player's rank across independent public draft boards
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.mechanism: Clubs' private boards are correlated with public expert boards, so the public consensus rank and its spread locate where a prospect is likely to come off the board.
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.rationale: A prospect ranked 3rd by every board has a narrow selection window; one ranked between 4th and 20th has a wide one, and exact-slot probability is driven as much by that disagreement as by the mean. Boards are expert scouting judgements, not prices, and they update through spring (college season, high-school showcases), so vintage matters.
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.measurement: Collect the final pre-draft top-250 lists from MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, ESPN, FanGraphs and The Athletic; for each prospect compute mean rank, median, standard deviation and min-max range across boards, plus the rank change over the last 30 days. Weight boards equally unless historical rank-to-pick error by source (2015-2025 drafts) says otherwise; store each board with its publication timestamp.
raw_data: board name, publication date, prospect, rank, position, school, age
mlb.prospect_consensus_board.why: Primary prior over a prospect's selection position; exact-slot and top-10 probabilities are both functions of where the player sits on boards and how much boards disagree.

mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.label: Final mock drafts and insider reports linking named prospects to specific clubs, including reported pre-draft bonus agreements
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.mechanism: In the last 48 hours before the draft, insiders report which club is on which player and which prospects agreed below-slot bonuses, and these links often fix top picks.
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.rationale: Top MLB picks are frequently pre-negotiated: the club and advisor agree a bonus before the pick, and national writers publish these links. A report that club X is 'in on' player Y at slot 5 can move the exact-slot probability far more than any scouting change. Mock drafts are writer forecasts, not market prices, but must be timestamped and scored for source accuracy.
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.measurement: Scrape every published mock and draft-day report from the final 14 days with timestamp, writer, slot, club and prospect; per writer compute historical exact-slot hit rate and top-10 hit rate over 2015-2025 first rounds with a Beta prior (k = 20 picks). Produce per prospect: share of final mocks placing him at each slot and a reliability-weighted slot distribution, frozen at the market snapshot timestamp.
raw_data: mock draft: writer, version timestamp, slot, club, prospect
draft-day report text with timestamp and claimed club link
club workouts and advisor-linked bonus reports
mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports.why: The most direct evidence of which club takes a prospect at which slot; exact-slot markets live or die on late club-player links and reported pre-draft deals.

mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.label: Prospect scouting and performance profile: tool grades, opponent-adjusted college or showcase stats, tracked batted-ball and pitch data, age and demographic class
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.mechanism: Clubs rank prospects by projected major-league value, which they build from tools, performance against level of competition, tracking data and age relative to class.
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.rationale: Analytic clubs weight college performance and age heavily (younger-for-class college hitters with strong contact and exit velocity rise), while scouting-led clubs weight tools and projection. Knowing why a prospect is ranked tells which clubs are likely to deviate from consensus on him, which matters at an exact slot.
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.measurement: For college players: wOBA, K% and BB% adjusted for conference strength, exit-velocity 90th percentile and chase rate from TrackMan or Synergy where published, and wood-bat summer league line (Cape Cod); for pitchers: velocity, spin, K-BB%. For high-school players: showcase metrics (exit velocity, 60-yard time, max fastball). Record age on draft day and class (HS, 4-year college, junior college); z-score each metric within class.
raw_data: college season lines by game with opponent
mlb.prospect_scouting_performance_profil.why: Explains the consensus rank and identifies prospects on whom analytics-led and scouting-led clubs disagree, widening or narrowing the slot window.

mlb.prospect_medical_signability.label: Prospect medical red flags and signability (college commitment leverage, advisor bonus demand, age-eligibility status)
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.mechanism: A prospect with a reported medical issue or a high bonus demand backed by a strong college commitment can slide well below his talent rank.
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.rationale: Pre-draft physicals (via the MLB Draft Combine medical program) and leaked bonus demands are classic causes of draft-day slides. High-school players can refuse to sign and go to college, so clubs avoid demanding players at slots whose value is below their ask; four-year college seniors have no leverage and go under slot.
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.measurement: For each prospect ranked in the consensus top 30 in the last 30 days before the draft: features = medical concern flag (reported, body part, surgery within 24 months), bonus ask over slot value at the consensus rank (ratio), commitment tier (top-25 program, other, junior college, none), age class (HS, 4-year junior, senior), agency historical over-slot rate. Target = actual pick minus consensus mean rank on 2012-2025 drafts (top 30 only). Fit ridge regression or ordinal logit with coefficients shrunk to zero with k = 20 prospects per feature; output expected slide in slots with its standard error and P(slide >= 5 slots). Units: slots. As-of: timestamped reports in the final 30 days; nothing published after the as-of time is used.
free_sources: MLB Pipeline and Baseball America draft reports (free_limited)
raw_data: report text and timestamp with medical or bonus-demand claims
mlb.prospect_medical_signability.why: Creates the left-skewed slide tail that makes 'top 10' fail for a highly ranked player and shifts exact-slot mass downward.

mlb.club_draft_tendency.label: Club drafting tendency at top picks: college vs high school, hitter vs pitcher, position, underslot frequency and deviation from consensus, by front-office regime
mlb.club_draft_tendency.mechanism: Each club picks from its own board; persistent front-office preferences make some clubs predictable deviators from consensus.
mlb.club_draft_tendency.rationale: Some clubs have taken college bats with nearly every high first-round pick, others take prep pitchers or reach for underslot deals to spread pool money. Tendencies hold only within a scouting director and general manager regime, so a regime change resets the prior.
mlb.club_draft_tendency.measurement: For each club, first-round and supplemental picks 2012-2025 restricted to the current scouting-director/GM tenure: share college, share pitcher, mean (pick slot minus consensus board rank), share signed below slot value. Shrink to league means with k = 6 picks; flag regime changes with the hire date.
raw_data: historical picks: year, slot, club, player, school type, position, signing bonus
mlb.club_draft_tendency.why: Conditional on the club at a slot, determines whether that club takes the consensus player or deviates, which is the crux of an exact-slot contract.

mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.label: Bonus-pool and slot-value structure: assigned slot values per pick, club pool size, overage tax and forfeiture thresholds, and incentives for underslot top picks
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.mechanism: Clubs maximise total draft value under a hard-ish bonus pool, so taking a cheaper player at a high slot frees money for later picks.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.rationale: Exceeding the pool by up to 5% costs a 75% tax and larger overages cost future first-round picks, so pools act as a budget constraint. Clubs with several early picks or a deep later class have strong incentives to sign the slot-5 pick below value, which favours college seniors and players with low leverage over the consensus talent.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.measurement: Per club and draft year (pool system from 2012): pool_total = sum of official slot values of the club's picks in rounds 1-10 as published before the draft, n_top75 = picks in slots 1-75, first_pick_share = first-pick slot value / pool_total. Historical discount for picks in slots 1-10 = (signed bonus - slot value) / slot value. underslot_score_c = share of the club's slot 1-10 picks signed below slot over the last 8 drafts, shrunk to the league share with k = 4 picks, a value in [0,1]. Record the CBA overage tax and pick-forfeiture tiers as constants and verify against the CBA text. Use only signings completed before the snapshot; the current class's bonuses are excluded. As-of: pool release and signings to date.
raw_data: official slot value by pick and year
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.why: Explains deviations from talent order at specific slots; underslot logic is why exact top-10 slots often go to players ranked lower on public boards.

mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.label: Sequential draft selection engine: club-specific rank-ordered choice over the remaining pool, giving P(prospect taken at slot k) and P(taken by slot N)
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.mechanism: The draft is a sequence of without-replacement choices: each club's choice depends on who remains, so pick probabilities across prospects and slots are jointly constrained.
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.rationale: Exact-slot probabilities for one prospect over slots 1..N plus P(not in top N) must sum to one, and across prospects each slot is taken by exactly one player. A rank-ordered (Plackett-Luce) choice model with club-specific utility shifts captures cascades: if two players go earlier than expected, the named player is more likely to fall to a given slot. It is a derived model that consumes the information inputs, so it is listed only as the structural constraint on them.
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.measurement: For slot k held by club c, choice probability over remaining prospects i is multinomial logit with U_ci = -alpha*rank_i + beta_c . x_i + gamma*report_shift_i - delta*risk_i, where rank_i = consensus rank at the as-of date (mean of MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, FanGraphs), x_i = (college, pitcher, underslot-fit) with club coefficients beta_c shrunk to the pooled coefficient with k = 6 picks, report_shift_i from mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports, risk_i = medical and signability flags. Fit alpha, beta, gamma, delta by maximum likelihood on 2012-2025 first rounds, using only pre-draft boards. Simulate the draft sequentially 50,000 times removing selected prospects; output P(prospect at slot k) and P(slot <= m). As-of: board and report snapshot with the final slot-owner map.
free_sources: derived from the inputs above and historical draft results (derived)
raw_data: historical first-round picks with pre-draft board ranks
current board, report and flag tables
mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model.why: Structural requirement, not an information source: the without-replacement engine that keeps slot and top-N probabilities for the two contracts mutually consistent; all information enters through the other inputs.

mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.reason: Only matters for markets open before the lottery draw; after the official order is released it is superseded by the slot-to-club map.

mlb.news_source_reliability_score.reason: Its reporter-accuracy logic transfers to draft insiders, but its calibration is on transaction reports; it needs re-estimation on mock-draft and draft-day link accuracy.

mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.reason: Relevant only through the ten-slot penalty for clubs far over the top tax threshold, which rarely touches slots 1-10; its payroll-space use for acquisitions is irrelevant here.

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.reason: The 2026 draft was held before the CBA expiry on 1 December 2026, but a lockout could postpone or shrink a 2027 draft, which the contract text does not address. Applies to 2027-draft series only; irrelevant to the finalized 2026 markets.

m.rules_text.reason: Exact-slot versus top-N wording defines the event; missing source and compensation-pick numbering must be tracked per draft year.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that a prospect goes at slot k is conditional on which club holds k: a club that takes college bats almost exclusively raises a college hitter's slot-k chance and lowers a prep pitcher's, independently of board rank.
interactions.how_to_test: In 2012-2025 first rounds, regress (pick minus consensus rank) on prospect class interacted with the picking club's prior college share; a significant interaction confirms conditionality.

interactions.mechanism: When boards agree (rank SD below about 2) the consensus rank predicts the slot well and insider links add little; when boards disagree, the selection is decided by club-specific links and reports dominate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare exact-slot log loss of consensus-only versus consensus-plus-final-mock models, split by cross-board rank SD tercile.

interactions.mechanism: A high bonus demand only causes a slide at slots held by clubs planning underslot deals; at slots held by clubs paying full slot it costs little, so slide risk is demand times the club's underslot propensity.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress slide (pick minus rank) on reported demand flag x picking-club underslot score among top-30 ranked prep players.

interactions.mechanism: A medical or demand flag moves a prospect differently by rank: a top-three player with a flag still goes inside the top 10, while a player ranked 6-12 with the same flag slides out of it, because no club at the top needs to take the risk.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress slide (pick minus consensus rank) on flag indicator interacted with consensus rank tercile among top-30 prospects in 2012-2025 drafts.

interactions.mechanism: A club-player link moves probability in proportion to the reporting writer's historical exact-slot hit rate; a link from a low-accuracy mock is close to noise.
interactions.how_to_test: Score writers' final mocks 2015-2025 by exact-slot hits and test whether reliability-weighted link shares beat equal-weight shares.

nonlinearities.shape: convex spread of selection window in mean rank
nonlinearities.why: Slot variance grows faster than linearly with mean rank: top-two prospects almost never fall more than two slots, while prospects ranked 8-15 can land anywhere from 4 to 30, so exact-slot probability decays steeply with rank.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: discrete slide when a flag is reported
nonlinearities.why: Medical or demand flags do not shift slot smoothly; a credible report removes the player from several clubs' boards at once, producing a jump of many slots rather than a proportional move.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in record rank via lottery cutoffs
nonlinearities.why: Lottery odds are flat among the worst three clubs and fall in steps; outside the lottery, order is deterministic, so a one-win difference in prior record can move a club across a step.

catalog_entry.label: Season maximum pitch velocity thresholds (player or league-wide)
catalog_entry.target: Whether a named pitcher, or any pitcher, throws a pitch at or above a velocity threshold (e.g. 107 MPH) in any game of the season including playoffs, per tracked pitch speed.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The season's fastest pitch is the maximum of a bounded per-pitch speed distribution taken over a few thousand near-peak fastballs from a small pool of elite throwers. Exceeding a threshold beyond the tracked record needs a pitcher whose ceiling sits close to it, enough max-effort attempts (relief use, postseason), favourable situations (rest, warmth, leverage), continued health and a tracking reading that lands above the line. The tail is bounded by physiology, so exceedance probabilities beyond the observed record fall off faster than an exponential tail would imply.

inputs.why: Identifies which arms have tracked peaks close enough to the threshold to matter.
Bounded-tail extreme-value engine that turns peaks and exposure into exceedance probability.
Remaining number of near-peak fastballs, including postseason weighted by qualification odds.
Starter pacing versus max-effort relief changes how close each pitch is to the ceiling.
Leverage, postseason, rest and temperature shift the upper tail for a given pitch.
Elite throwers lose exposure to arm injury, eroding the candidate pool.
Recent velocity trajectory shows whether a candidate is near or below his peak form.
Current IL status with point-in-time vintage zeroes near-term exposure.
Park offsets, data revisions and rounding decide borderline readings.
Game-time temperature feeds the situational lift on velocity.
Short postseason leashes and high-leverage bullpen use raise near-peak attempts.
Workload caps on young hard throwers truncate appearances and near-peak exposure.
Threshold, inclusion of playoffs and named-versus-any construction.
Frequency of glitch or mis-tagged readings in the raw live feed and how fast they are corrected; a non-physical route to a 107 reading.

interactions.hypothesis: Exceedance requires both a near-threshold ceiling and many attempts; volume without ceiling contributes almost nothing, so the two multiply inside the tail.
Postseason bullpen use of hard-throwing starters converts paced pitches into max-effort pitches, concentrating record chances in October.
The situational lift (temperature included as a fixed effect) shifts the per-pitch mean, and at a threshold beyond the record a small additive lift multiplies the tail probability.
A falling velocity trend signals elevated injury hazard, so exposure loss and lower ceiling arrive together rather than independently.

contract.settlement_definition: KXMLBFASTPITCH settles YES if the named pitcher (sample: Jacob Misiorowski) records a pitch at or above the strike (107.0 MPH) in any game of the stated season, regular season and playoffs included; KXMLBSTAT (sample) settles YES if any pitcher records a 107+ MPH pitch in any game of the season including playoffs. A single pitch suffices. The text does not name the tracking source, does not define how a reading like 106.95 is rounded, and does not say whether spring training, exhibitions or All-Star Game pitches count. KXMLBSTAT is not velocity-only (verified 2026-11-08 from the Kalshi events and markets endpoints): its 2026 events are 105+, 106+ and 107+ MPH pitch; a 500+ foot home run 'per Statcast measurement'; any hitter with 50+ HR and 50+ SB in the regular season; 2+ grand slams in a game; 4+ home runs in a game; any pitcher with 20+ regular-season wins; 20+ strikeouts in a game; an individual no-hitter (a combined no-hitter does not count); and a perfect game. The single-game and distance events count regular season and playoffs; the 50/50 and 20-win events count the regular season only.

rules_evidence.quote: If Jacob Misiorowski records a 107.0+ MPH pitch in any game during the 2026 Pro Baseball season (regular season and playoffs), then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Named-pitcher, one-pitch threshold at 107.0 with one decimal; window is the full season including playoffs.

rules_evidence.quote: If any pitcher records a 107+ MPH Pitch in any game during the 2026 Pro Baseball season (regular season and playoffs)
rules_evidence.establishes: League-wide union over all pitchers; threshold written '107+' without the decimal; same season-plus-playoffs window.

variants_and_edge_cases: Named-pitcher (KXMLBFASTPITCH, ladder strikes via floor_strike 107 with greater_or_equal) versus any-pitcher (KXMLBSTAT, custom strike) construction; P(any) >= P(named) for the same threshold.
'107.0+' versus '107+': whether a reading displayed as 107.0 after rounding from 106.95-106.99 counts is not defined.
'any game during the ... season (regular season and playoffs)' leaves spring training and the All-Star Game unaddressed; a position player pitching also counts as 'any pitcher'.
No resolution source is named (Statcast release speed versus stadium radar or broadcast readings can differ), and later data revisions are not addressed.

KXMLBSTAT is a generic season-stat series; this record covers it only for velocity markets such as KXMLBSTAT-26P107-AP, other KXMLBSTAT markets may settle on different stats and are recorded in series_mapping_issues.
A reading published in the live feed or broadcast and later corrected or removed: whether it counts is unstated (velo_first_vs_revised_reading).

Non-velocity KXMLBSTAT events (verified list): rare single-game feats (no-hitter by one pitcher only, perfect game, 4+ HR game, 20+ K game, 2+ grand slams, 500+ ft Statcast HR) over regular season plus playoffs, and season thresholds (20+ wins, 50 HR plus 50 SB) over the regular season only; all are 'any player' unions, so they are league-wide hazards rather than named-player markets.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named; presumed MLB Statcast (Hawk-Eye) release speed as published on Baseball Savant / MLB game feed.

series_mapping_issues.issue: Verified 2026-11-08: 8 of 11 KXMLBSTAT events settle on non-velocity stats (500 ft HR, 50/50, 2 grand slams, 4 HR game, 20 wins, 20 K game, individual no-hitter, perfect game). They are now covered in this record by stage s6 with their own inputs; a dedicated league-wide season-feats archetype would still be a cleaner filing.

mechanism.summary: A velocity-threshold contract settles on the single fastest tracked pitch, so it is an extreme-value problem on a physically bounded quantity. Each pitcher has a speed ceiling set by his arm; only a handful sit within two mph of the threshold, and 107 mph is beyond any tracked pitch to date. Within a pitcher, each fastball's speed equals his current baseline plus situational lifts (leverage, postseason adrenaline, rest, warm air, early in the outing) minus fatigue and paced effort as a starter. The probability of crossing the line is roughly one minus the product, over the remaining near-peak fastballs, of the chance each stays below, so volume of max-effort pitches and health (exposure) multiply the per-pitch tail. Finally the reading itself is a measurement with park calibration error and rounding, which matters at the edge, and with the line above any tracked pitch a gross feed error that is published, and perhaps later corrected, may be a more probable route to YES than the physical tail. The archetype also holds the eight non-velocity KXMLBSTAT events (league-wide season feats, stage s6) because series_assignment files the whole series here; they share no mechanism with release speed and would belong in a separate season-feats archetype, which this pass cannot create.

stages.name: Candidate pool and arm ceiling
stages.description: Identify the pitchers whose tracked peaks lie close to the threshold: current MLB relievers and starters with season maxima of 103 mph and higher, plus AAA prospects with tracked peaks that could be called up. Each candidate's ceiling drifts with age, mechanics and health. Because the distribution of pitcher ceilings has a hard upper edge, the any-pitcher probability is carried by two or three arms at most.
stages.distribution: Bounded upper tail (Weibull-domain extreme value with a finite endpoint); pool size is a small discrete count of arms.

stages.name: Health, role and remaining exposure
stages.description: For each candidate, how many near-peak fastballs remain: games left, his role (one-inning closer versus paced starter), the chance of a role change, workload caps, IL status and the forward hazard of an arm injury, and postseason games weighted by his club's probability of playing them. Exposure shrinks over the season and collapses for a candidate who is shut down.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated count of near-peak fastballs; heavy left mass from injury shutdowns; postseason adds a lumpy mixture over rounds.

stages.name: Per-pitch speed given situation
stages.description: Each fastball's speed is the pitcher's baseline for that day plus lifts for leverage, postseason, days of rest, pitch number within the appearance, two-strike counts and temperature. Record-level pitches occur in a narrow set of situations: rested, warm, high-leverage or playoff, first few pitches of an appearance. Small additive lifts change the tail probability by large factors.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal body per pitcher-day with a short, bounded right tail; day-level random effect induces correlation among pitches in one outing.

stages.name: Extreme aggregation over the season
stages.description: Combine per-pitch exceedance probabilities across all remaining near-peak pitches and candidates: P(named) = 1 - product over his pitches of (1 - p), P(any) = 1 - product over candidates. Pitches within a day and pitchers sharing parks or calibration are not independent, and fitting a tail beyond the observed record needs a bounded generalised-Pareto shape rather than an exponential extrapolation.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcome from a max over thousands of correlated draws; probability highly sensitive to the tail shape parameter near the endpoint.

stages.name: Measurement and settlement
stages.description: The deciding reading is a Hawk-Eye release-speed measurement with park-specific offsets, possible post-game revision and one-decimal display; the named series uses 107.0+, the any-pitcher series 107+. The rules include playoffs but do not name a source, so a stadium radar or broadcast figure above 107 that Statcast does not confirm is an unresolved edge. A second route to YES is non-physical: a glitch or mis-tagged speed in the live feed that is published at game time and later corrected, whose settlement treatment is unstated.
stages.distribution: Small symmetric measurement error of a few tenths of a mph, decisive only near the line, plus a rare heavy-tailed gross-error component (feed glitches, mis-tags) that can dominate P(YES) when the physical tail is near zero.

stages.name: Non-velocity KXMLBSTAT feats: rare single-game events and season thresholds
stages.description: The same series also lists league-wide feats that share nothing with release speed. Single-game feats (an individual no-hitter, a perfect game, four home runs or two grand slams by one hitter, twenty strikeouts, a 500-foot drive by Statcast) are unions over every remaining team-game of a tiny per-game rate set by the league strikeout and power environment and by how long starters work; playoff games count. Season thresholds (20 pitcher wins, 50 HR plus 50 SB) are regular-season races of the few candidates on pace, decided by remaining starts or plate appearances. Each is settled Yes the moment the feat occurs.
stages.distribution: Low-rate Poisson survival over remaining games for single-game feats (season probabilities range from small for a 20-strikeout game or a perfect game to large for at least one individual no-hitter); for season thresholds, a union over two or three candidates whose probabilities fall to zero once the pace is lost.

talent_strength.note: Arm ceiling and its current trajectory.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing hitters do not change release speed beyond the leverage of the moment, which is carried by the situational lift; batter identity has no direct mechanism on velocity.

role_personnel.note: Starter versus reliever effort regime and who is in the pool.

availability_news.note: Current IL status and forward arm-injury hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: Club workload caps and role decisions.

environment.note: Temperature effect on velocity, applied through the situational lift.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-pitch exceedance probability is the conversion rate of attempts into a qualifying reading.

distribution_variance.note: Bounded extreme-value tail with within-day correlation.

officiating_rules.note: Tracking calibration and revisions act as the 'official' of this contract.

settlement_contract.note: Threshold wording, playoffs included, source unnamed. First-published versus corrected reading is unstated (velo_first_vs_revised_reading).

mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.label: Candidate pool of pitchers able to approach the velocity threshold: tracked peak velocity, top-pitch distribution and minor-league peaks of possible call-ups
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.mechanism: Only pitchers whose tracked peak already sits within roughly two mph of the threshold have any realistic chance of a single pitch exceeding it.
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.rationale: Pitch speed is bounded by the arm: league-wide, fewer than a dozen pitchers have tracked pitches above 104 mph in a season, and the all-time tracked maxima sit near 105-106 mph. For the 'any pitcher' series the pool, not the average pitcher, carries the probability; prospects with Statcast-tracked AAA peaks can join it mid-season.
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.measurement: From Statcast pitch-level release_speed (MLB) and Hawk-Eye AAA data: for each pitcher in the last three seasons compute season max, 99.9th and 99th percentile of fastball speed, number of pitches at or above 103 and 104 mph, and age; include in the pool if 3-season max >= 103.0 mph or AAA max >= 103.0. Apply an aging adjustment of about -0.2 to -0.3 mph per year after age 27 to percentiles, shrunk by pitch counts. As-of: daily.
raw_data: pitch-level: pitcher, date, game_pk, pitch_type, release_speed, level
mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool.why: Defines who can plausibly reach 107 and how far each is from it; the named-pitcher series is one pool member, the any-pitcher series the union.

mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.label: Remaining exposure to max-effort fastballs: expected count of high-velocity fastballs per candidate over the rest of the season and postseason
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.mechanism: The chance that the season maximum crosses a threshold rises with the number of near-peak attempts, so exposure is the volume term of the extreme.
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.rationale: A closer throws perhaps 600-900 fastballs a year, nearly all at full effort; a starter throws more but paces, so only first-inning and high-leverage fastballs approach his ceiling. Exposure must count near-peak attempts, not all pitches, and must add postseason games only with the team's probability of playing them.
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.measurement: Per candidate: projected remaining appearances (role, health) x fastballs per appearance x share of fastballs within 1.5 mph of his season max (from his own pitch-level data, last 60 days with shrinkage to prior season, k = 300 pitches); add postseason expected appearances = P(team reaches each round) x expected games x appearance rate. Units: expected near-peak fastballs. As-of: daily.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule and standings (free)
raw_data: pitch-level fastball speeds with appearance id
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.why: Converts per-pitch tail probability into a season probability; late-season markets shrink sharply as exposure runs out.

mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.label: Within-pitcher situational velocity lift: change in fastball speed with leverage, postseason, inning of appearance, pitch number, count, days of rest and temperature
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.mechanism: A pitcher's top speed on a given pitch is his baseline plus situational lifts; record pitches cluster in high-adrenaline, rested, warm, early-in-outing situations.
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.rationale: Velocity rises in the postseason and in high-leverage spots, falls after consecutive days of work and with pitch count, and is expected to be lower in colder air (effect size unverified, see velo_temperature_effect). Because the threshold sits in the extreme tail, a lift of half a mph multiplies the exceedance probability many times.
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.measurement: Mixed model: release_speed (four-seam and sinker) ~ pitcher random intercept + pitcher-by-season random slope on pitch number + fixed effects: leverage index bucket (<0.85, 0.85-2.0, >2.0), postseason flag, pitch number within appearance (natural spline, 3 df), two-strike flag, days since last appearance (0, 1, 2, 3+), game temperature in F (linear, centered 70), roof-closed flag. Fit by REML on all regular and postseason pitches from the 4 seasons before the as-of date only. Output per-situation additive lift in mph with standard errors, added to a pitcher's baseline speed distribution location parameter (scale unchanged). Units: mph. As-of: refit each offseason, recomputed preseason; no data dated after the as-of used.
free_sources: MLB Stats API game weather fields (free)
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed with game_pk, inning, pitch number, count
leverage index (computed from base-out and score state)
mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift.why: The threshold is crossed in particular situations; lifts shift the whole upper tail and are the main driver of week-to-week change in exceedance probability.

mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.label: Pitch-speed tracking calibration: Hawk-Eye release-speed definition, park-level speed offsets, data revisions and displayed precision
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.mechanism: A record pitch is a measurement; park-to-park calibration offsets and later corrections can move a reading by a few tenths of a mph, which is decisive at the edge.
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.rationale: Statcast reports release speed, which differs from the old PITCHf/x 50-ft reading, so historical records are not directly comparable. Park-specific biases have been documented for radar systems, scoreboard and broadcast readings differ from Statcast, and MLB sometimes revises pitch data after the game. Settlement on '107.0+' versus '107+' interacts with one-decimal rounding.
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.measurement: For each park and season estimate the speed offset as the mean residual of visiting pitchers' fastball speeds at that park versus their speeds elsewhere (pitcher fixed effects, minimum 2,000 pitches per park-season, shrink to zero with k = 5,000). Track revisions by re-pulling pitch data 1, 7 and 30 days after each game and recording changes in release_speed. Record displayed precision (one decimal).
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed by park and game
repeated pulls of the same games at different dates
mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration.why: Determines whether a borderline 106.9-107.1 reading settles YES, and adjusts candidate tail fits for park bias.

mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.label: Forward injury hazard for elite-velocity pitchers: probability of losing the remaining season to elbow or shoulder injury, conditional on velocity and workload history
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.mechanism: The pitchers who could set a velocity record are the ones most exposed to UCL and shoulder injuries, so the pool erodes during the season.
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.rationale: Current IL status is not enough: the question is how much of the remaining exposure each candidate will actually pitch. Velocity is a known risk factor for elbow injury, and a velocity drop is often the first sign. The named pitcher's market is near zero if he is shut down; the any-pitcher market loses its tail contributors one by one.
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time hazard per 30-day window of a 60+ day IL placement for elbow or shoulder, fitted on 2015-2025 pitchers with covariates: peak fastball velocity, age, prior UCL surgery, innings in prior 12 months, recent velocity z-score drop (from rolling starts); output expected share of remaining exposure lost. Point-in-time: use only IL transactions and velocity known at the as-of date.
free_sources: Jon Roegele Tommy John surgery list (free)
raw_data: IL transactions with dates and body part
mlb.hard_thrower_injury_hazard.why: Shrinks remaining exposure for each candidate; for the named-pitcher series it is often the dominant way the market resolves NO early.

mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.label: Pitcher role and effort regime: starter pacing versus one-inning max-effort relief, and probability of a role change (including postseason bullpen use of starters)
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.mechanism: Starters pace velocity over 90-100 pitches while one-inning relievers throw every pitch near peak, so the same arm reaches higher speeds in relief.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.rationale: A hard-throwing starter typically sits 1.5-3 mph above his starting average when used in short relief. Postseason clubs often move starters to the bullpen, and clubs sometimes convert prospects to relief. The named-pitcher probability depends on which role he will occupy for how many appearances.
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.measurement: Role = SP if the pitcher started the last start, RP otherwise, opener if started and faced <=6 batters. P(role change before date) = logistic on prior role, days since last start/relief appearance, team playoff status, IL status and any dated manager statement flag, fit on 2015-2025 role switches with ridge penalty. Speed shift = within-pitcher difference in 99th percentile fastball speed between relief and starting appearances, estimated on pitchers with >=100 fastballs in each role, shrunk to the league mean shift with k = 15 pitchers' equivalents of 100 fastballs. Output role-weighted 99th percentile speed = P(role) weighted mix, and expected appearances by role. Units: mph and appearances. As-of: daily.
raw_data: appearance logs with role (start/relief) and innings
mlb.pitcher_role_effort_regime.why: Role decides how close each pitch is to the arm's ceiling; a starter moved to relief in October is the most plausible record setter.

mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.label: Frequency and persistence of anomalous release-speed readings in the raw live tracking feed versus the later corrected Statcast record
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.mechanism: With 107 mph above every tracked pitch, a YES can come from a feed glitch, mis-tagged pitch or unit error that is published (and possibly later corrected) rather than from a physical pitch.
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.rationale: The physical tail near 107 is almost empty, so the probability of a spurious reading can dominate the physical path. What counts depends on whether Kalshi settles on the first published reading or the corrected one, which the rules do not say. Calibration of Savant re-pulls alone cannot see readings that were removed before the first public pull.
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.measurement: Poll the MLB Stats API live game feed for every game during play and store each pitch's startSpeed with capture timestamp and pitch id; after 1, 7 and 30 days re-pull Savant release_speed for the same pitch. Per season compute: (a) count of live-feed pitches with speed >= 104.0 or more than 3.0 mph above that pitcher's season 99th percentile, (b) share of those that changed by more than 1.0 mph or vanished in later pulls, (c) median hours to correction. Output an expected number of anomalous readings >= threshold per season, with a Beta(0.5,0.5) prior on the per-game rate. As-of: daily, own-captured snapshots only.
free_sources: MLB Stats API live game feed polling (own_capture)
raw_data: live-feed pitch snapshots with capture timestamp
mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate.why: Captures the non-physical path to a 107 reading and its correction latency, which the park-offset and revision inputs cannot see; it sets a floor under P(any pitcher 107+) that the extreme-value engine alone would miss.

mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard.label: League-wide single-game rare-event hazard over the remaining season and playoffs (individual no-hitter, perfect game, 4+ HR game, 20+ K game, 2+ grand slams in a game, 500+ ft Statcast home run)
mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard.mechanism: Each 'any player' feat is a union over every remaining team-game of a tiny per-game probability, so its chance is one minus the survival of a low-rate point process whose rate depends on the league's strikeout and power environment and on how long starters pitch.
mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard.rationale: Rates moved sharply across eras: higher strikeout rates raised no-hit and 20-strikeout chances per inning while shorter starts lowered the chance of one pitcher finishing 27 outs, and only individual no-hitters count here; multi-HR feats depend on the right tail of hitter power, and 500-foot drives depend on the Statcast distance tail and altitude (Coors Field). Using long-run historical averages without these adjustments misstates the hazard by large factors.
mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard.measurement: For event e, per team-game rate lambda_e(t) = exp(b0_e + b1_e*league K% + b2_e*league HR per PA + b3_e*league mean starter outs per start) fitted by Poisson regression on league-season counts 1990-2025 (500 ft: Statcast seasons 2015-2025 only, count of HR with hit_distance_sc >= 500); for the individual no-hitter count only games where one pitcher recorded all outs; covariates are season-to-date values at the as-of date. Multi-HR and 2-grand-slam feats are cross-checked bottom-up: sum over hitter-games of P(4+ HR) or P(2+ GS) from each hitter's per-PA HR rate (mlb.hitter_hr_profile) with 4.2 PA per game. The 500 ft term uses a generalised Pareto tail fitted to HR distances >= 450 ft with a park altitude covariate. P(event in the rest of the season) = 1 - exp(-sum over remaining regular-season team-games and expected playoff games of lambda_e). Units: probability; as-of the market timestamp with games already played counted as observed (a feat already achieved settles Yes).
free_sources: Retrosheet game logs and event files (no-hitters, multi-HR games, strikeouts per game)
Baseball-Reference no-hitter, perfect game and multi-HR game lists
Baseball Savant Statcast hit_distance_sc for home runs (2015+)
raw_data: league-season counts of individual no-hitters, perfect games, 4+ HR games, 20+ K games, 2+ GS games, 500+ ft HR
league-season K%, HR per PA, starter outs per start
mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard.why: Eight of the eleven KXMLBSTAT events are league-wide rare feats, not velocity extremes; they need a per-game hazard over the remaining schedule, not the velocity tail engine.

mlb.any_pitcher_season_wins_threshold.label: Any-pitcher 20-win season threshold: probability at least one pitcher reaches 20 regular-season wins
mlb.any_pitcher_season_wins_threshold.mechanism: A pitcher's wins accumulate one start at a time with a win credited only if he completes five innings with his team leading and the lead holds, so 20 wins needs a near-full rotation workload on a strong team and has become rare as starts shorten.
mlb.any_pitcher_season_wins_threshold.rationale: Wins depend on team offence and bullpen as much as on the pitcher, and on starts remaining; the union over pitchers is dominated by the two or three leaders by the deadline, and the event collapses once their remaining starts cannot close the gap, so a pace-based projection that ignores remaining rotation turns misprices it late in the season.
mlb.any_pitcher_season_wins_threshold.measurement: For each pitcher with W0 wins at the as-of date: remaining starts n_i from the rotation schedule (mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest, five-man turns adjusted for off days and IL risk); per-start win probability p_i = P(starter records >= 15 outs) from the shared exit hazard (mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve) x P(team leads when he exits and holds the lead) from his team's run-scoring and bullpen models, fitted on 2015-2025 starts with logistic calibration. W_i = W0 + Binomial(n_i, p_i) (Poisson-binomial when p varies by opponent); P(any >= 20) = 1 - product over pitchers of P(W_i < 20), assuming independence across teams and a shared-team correction for teammates. Units: probability; as-of the market timestamp, regular season only per the rules.
free_sources: MLB Stats API player game logs and probable pitchers
Retrosheet start logs for win-credit calibration
raw_data: pitcher season wins and starts to date
start logs with outs recorded, score at exit and final decision
mlb.any_pitcher_season_wins_threshold.why: KXMLBSTAT-26W20-AP is a season threshold on wins, which the velocity inputs do not touch.

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR_0, SB_0, team games remaining G, per-game play probability from availability and PA per game by lineup slot, set rates r_HR and r_SB per PA = (ROS projection * 250 + season pace * n)/(250 + n) with n = season PA. Simulate 20,000 seasons: PA_rest from game draws with a health hazard; HR_rest ~ NegBin(mean r_HR*PA_rest, dispersion fitted across hitters 2015-2025) and SB_rest ~ NegBin(mean r_SB*PA_rest); couple the two with a Gaussian copula whose rho is the cross-hitter correlation of season HR and SB rate residuals given PA (2015-2025). Output P(HR_0 + HR_rest >= H* and SB_0 + SB_rest >= S*) for contract thresholds. As-of: daily.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.why: KXMLBSTAT-265050-AH asks whether any hitter reaches 50 HR and 50 SB in the regular season; the joint power-speed season distribution per candidate, unioned over the two or three hitters with a live pace, prices it.

mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.reason: The right engine, but its exponential-tail fit beyond the record and independence across pitchers overstate probability; it must use a bounded tail and the new exposure and lift inputs.

mlb.velo_trend.reason: Rolling velocity z-scores show whether a candidate is at peak form or declining, but it measures averages, not the top-pitch tail that settles this contract.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: Current IL status gates near-term exposure; it says nothing about the forward chance of a season-ending injury, which the new hazard input covers.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Only temperature matters, and only through a small per-pitch lift; wind and precipitation are irrelevant to release speed. It is a data feed of the situational lift (temperature fixed effect), not an independently interacting input.

mlb.postseason_leverage_usage.reason: Usage side only: how many max-effort appearances a postseason club gives candidates; the per-pitch speed effect of a postseason flag or leverage bucket sits in pitch_speed_situational_lift, so the two do not double count. Irrelevant for pitchers on non-contenders.

m.rules_text.reason: Threshold value and decimal, named versus any pitcher and playoff inclusion all come from the wording.

mlb.pitch_count_limit.reason: Workload caps for young flamethrowers truncate appearances and cut near-peak exposure, but caps rarely bind on one-inning relievers, so this is context rather than a secondary driver.

interactions.mechanism: Season exceedance is roughly 1 - exp(-N x p): N near-peak pitches times the per-pitch tail p given the ceiling. A pitcher topping out 3 mph below the line has p near zero, so even thousands of pitches add nothing; exposure only matters for arms whose ceiling is close.
interactions.how_to_test: Across 2015-2025, regress whether a pitcher's season max exceeded his prior-season 99.9th percentile by 1 mph on log near-peak pitch count interacted with distance from that percentile.

interactions.mechanism: A starter moved to the October bullpen switches from paced effort to max effort, raising his top-speed distribution by one to three mph for the remaining appearances; regular-season starter exposure says little about this regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare within-pitcher 99th-percentile fastball speed in postseason relief versus regular-season starts for starters used in relief in 2015-2025 postseasons.

interactions.mechanism: An additive lift (leverage, rest, temperature, all fixed effects inside the lift input) shifts the per-pitch distribution, and because the threshold sits in the bounded tail, tail probability rises convexly with the lift until close to the endpoint.
interactions.how_to_test: Count pitches above each pitcher's personal 99.9th percentile by temperature and leverage bins; check that the ratio grows faster than the mean speed shift.

interactions.mechanism: Velocity decline and injury tend to arrive together, so a falling trend lowers both the ceiling and the expected remaining exposure; treating them as independent overstates the probability for declining candidates.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether a velocity z-score drop in the last three appearances predicts a 60+ day IL stint within 30 days, controlling for age and workload.

interactions.mechanism: Park speed offsets bias a candidate's measured ceiling depending on where he pitches; a closer whose home park reads hot appears closer to the threshold, and the contract settles on that biased reading.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare candidates' home and road 99th-percentile speeds after removing league-wide park offsets estimated from visiting pitchers.

interactions.mechanism: When the best candidate ceilings sit more than about 2 mph under the line the physical exceedance probability is near zero and the anomaly rate sets P(YES); only when a candidate's ceiling approaches the line does the physical tail dominate, so the weight on each route switches with the ceiling gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Across seasons, compare the count of live-feed readings above 105 mph that survive in corrected Savant data against the count of physical pitches above 104.5; check which grows with ceiling gap.

interactions.mechanism: Both feats depend on how deep starters pitch: the league trend toward shorter starts lowers the chance that one pitcher records all outs of a no-hitter and also lowers the number of five-inning starts that can earn wins, so a season with a lower starter-outs mean shifts both probabilities down together while raising nothing comparable.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress league-season individual no-hitter counts and 20-win pitcher counts on mean starter outs per start; joint residual correlation across 1990-2025 shows the shared dependence.

nonlinearities.shape: near-zero then sharply rising, bounded tail in distance to threshold
nonlinearities.why: Exceedance probability is effectively zero for ceilings more than about two mph below the line and rises steeply over the last mph, so a 0.5 mph change in a candidate's peak can change the season probability by an order of magnitude.

Additional near-peak pitches add diminishing probability once N x p is large; for this threshold N x p is tiny, so the response is nearly linear and exposure late in the season matters proportionally.
Measurement error matters only for readings within a few tenths of 107.0; one-decimal rounding and the 107.0+ versus 107+ wording create a step around the line.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave saturating in remaining team-games: 1 - exp(-lambda * games)
nonlinearities.why: Early in the season a no-hitter is near certain over the full schedule while a perfect game or 4-HR game remains unlikely; the probability rises steeply then saturates as games accumulate, and drops to the realised outcome once the window closes.

unresolved.description: The rules name no tracking source and do not define rounding: '107.0+' (named) and '107+' (any) may treat a 106.95 reading differently, and stadium or broadcast radar readings could conflict with Statcast.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rules_secondary or clarification naming Statcast release speed and its precision.

unresolved.description: 107 mph lies beyond every tracked pitch; any probability is an extrapolation whose value depends almost entirely on the assumed tail endpoint, which cannot be estimated from data.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Biomechanical evidence on the physical ceiling of arm speed or a sensitivity analysis over generalised-Pareto shape parameters.

unresolved.description: 'any game during the season (regular season and playoffs)' does not say whether spring training, the All-Star Game or suspended-game completions count, nor whether World Baseball Classic or other non-MLB games pitched by MLB arms (which tracking systems record) count; the 'Pro Baseball season' wording most plausibly excludes them.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Full rules text or a settlement note listing included game types.
